learn: Earth's systems are the geosphere (rock), hydrosphere (water), atmosphere (air) and biosphere (life).
Matter and energy flow between spheres.
A volcanic eruption affects all four spheres.
lessons.try: Diagram how a hurricane involves all four spheres.

learn: The Sun drives weather, the water cycle and photosynthesis.
Earth's internal heat (from formation and radioactive decay) drives plate tectonics.
Gravity shapes tides and erosion.
lessons.try: Classify ten Earth processes by their energy source.

learn: Positive feedback amplifies change; negative feedback reduces it.
Melting ice lowers reflectivity (albedo), causing more warming: positive feedback.
Systems thinking reveals connections.
check: Melting ice causing more warming is ___ feedback.
lessons.try: Draw a feedback loop for Arctic ice melt.

learn: Layers: crust, mantle, outer core (liquid), inner core (solid).
The lithosphere (crust and upper mantle) is broken into plates.
Seismic waves reveal the interior: S waves cannot pass through liquid.
lessons.try: Build a scale model of Earth's layers.

learn: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912.
Evidence: matching coastlines, fossils, rocks, and seafloor magnetic stripes.
Seafloor spreading at mid-ocean ridges creates new crust.
lessons.try: Match fossil evidence across continents on a map.

learn: Divergent: plates move apart (Mid-Atlantic Ridge). Convergent: plates collide (Himalayas, Andes). Transform: plates slide past (San Andreas Fault).
Subduction creates trenches and volcanoes.
Earthquakes and volcanoes cluster at boundaries, such as the Ring of Fire.
check: The San Andreas Fault is a ___ boundary.
The Himalayas formed at a ___ boundary.
The Ring of Fire surrounds the...
lessons.try: Map earthquakes and volcanoes and identify boundaries.

units.t: Rocks, Minerals and the Rock Cycle

learn: Minerals are natural, inorganic, crystalline solids with definite composition.
Identify by hardness (Mohs scale), streak, lustre, cleavage and colour.
Quartz and feldspar are the most common crustal minerals.
check: The hardest mineral on the Mohs scale is...
Streak is the colour of a mineral's...
lessons.try: Identify mineral samples using a key.

learn: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava (granite, basalt).
Sedimentary rocks form from compacted sediments (sandstone, limestone).
Metamorphic rocks form under heat and pressure (marble, slate).
check: Fossils are usually found in ___ rock.
lessons.try: Classify ten rock samples.

learn: Rocks change type through melting, cooling, weathering, erosion, deposition, heat and pressure.
The cycle takes millions of years.
Weathering is physical or chemical.
lessons.try: Draw the rock cycle with arrows labelled by process.

learn: Superposition: lower layers are older.
Cross-cutting: a feature cutting layers is younger.
Index fossils date layers.
check: In undisturbed layers, the bottom is...
lessons.try: Sequence events in a rock layer diagram.

learn: Radiometric dating uses decay rates of isotopes.
Uranium-lead dates very old rocks; carbon-14 dates remains under about 50,000 years.
Earth is about 4.6 billion years old.
lessons.try: Solve half-life dating problems.

learn: Eons, eras, periods and epochs divide Earth's history.
Eras: Paleozoic, Mesozoic (dinosaurs), Cenozoic (mammals).
Mass extinctions mark boundaries; an asteroid ended the Cretaceous 66 million years ago.
check: The Cretaceous ended about ___ years ago.
lessons.try: Make a scaled timeline of Earth's history on a long strip.

learn: Layers: troposphere (weather), stratosphere (ozone), mesosphere, thermosphere.
Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
The ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation.
lessons.try: Graph temperature against altitude through the layers.

learn: Air masses are large bodies of air with similar temperature and humidity.
Cold fronts bring quick storms; warm fronts bring steady rain.
High pressure usually means fair weather; low pressure brings clouds and storms.
lessons.try: Read a weather map and forecast tomorrow's weather.

learn: Thunderstorms form from rising warm, moist air.
Hurricanes form over warm oceans; tornadoes form in severe thunderstorms.
Follow official warnings and have a safety plan.
check: In a tornado warning, go to a...
lessons.try: Make a severe weather safety plan for your family.

learn: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration and runoff move water.
About 97% of Earth's water is salty ocean.
Most fresh water is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.
check: About ___ of Earth's water is in oceans.
lessons.try: Model the water cycle in a sealed container.

learn: Surface currents are driven by wind; deep currents by density (temperature and salinity).
The global conveyor belt moves heat around the planet.
The Gulf Stream warms western Europe.
lessons.try: Trace the global conveyor belt on a map.

learn: Features: continental shelf, abyssal plain, trenches (Mariana Trench about 11 km deep).
Coral reefs hold great biodiversity.
Ocean acidification from absorbed CO₂ harms shell-building animals.
check: The Mariana Trench is about ___ deep.
lessons.try: Research a marine ecosystem and its threats.

learn: Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term average (30+ years).
Climate depends on latitude, altitude, ocean currents and landforms.
Climate zones: tropical, dry, temperate, continental, polar.
check: Climate is measured over about ___ years.
lessons.try: Compare the climates of two cities using climate graphs.

learn: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, methane, water vapour) trap heat.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth habitable.
Burning fossil fuels has raised CO₂ from about 280 ppm before industry to over 420 ppm today.
lessons.try: Graph CO₂ data from the Mauna Loa record.

learn: Evidence: rising temperatures, melting ice, rising seas, ice cores.
Impacts: heatwaves, droughts, floods, ecosystem shifts.
Mitigation reduces emissions; adaptation prepares for change.
lessons.try: Propose one mitigation and one adaptation for your community.

learn: Producers capture sunlight; consumers eat other organisms; decomposers recycle matter.
Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.
Food webs show feeding relationships.
check: About ___ of energy passes up each level.
lessons.try: Build a food web for a local ecosystem.

learn: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycle through living and non-living parts.
Photosynthesis removes CO₂; respiration and combustion release it.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria make nitrogen usable for plants.
lessons.try: Diagram the carbon cycle.

learn: Biodiversity includes genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.
Threats: habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, overharvesting, climate change (HIPPO).
Protected areas and restoration help.
check: The biggest threat to biodiversity is usually...
lessons.try: Research an endangered species and a recovery plan.

learn: Non-renewable: coal, oil, natural gas, uranium.
Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass.
Each has costs and benefits.
lessons.try: Compare the pros and cons of five energy sources.

learn: Mining provides metals but disturbs land.
Groundwater is stored in aquifers; overuse lowers water tables.
Recycling metals saves energy.
lessons.try: Calculate your household water use for a day.

learn: Efficiency reduces energy waste: insulation, LED lights, efficient appliances.
Electric transport and public transit cut emissions.
Conservation is often the cheapest energy source.
check: LEDs use ___ energy than old bulbs.
lessons.try: Do an energy audit of your home or school.

learn: Air pollution (particulates, smog), water pollution (runoff, sewage), soil pollution and plastic.
Microplastics have been found throughout the oceans.
Laws like the Clean Air Act have improved air quality.
lessons.try: Monitor air quality data for your area for a week.

learn: Earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunamis, floods, landslides and wildfires.
Scientists monitor hazards and issue warnings.
Building codes and planning reduce damage.
lessons.try: Assess hazards for your region and the local response plan.

learn: Sustainability meets present needs without harming future generations.
Reduce, reuse, recycle; design products for long life.
Individual, community and government actions all matter.
lessons.try: Design a sustainability project for your school.
